draft.title: Five-number summary and IQR
card: Put the data in order. The five-number summary is the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and maximum.
The median splits the ordered data into a lower half and an upper half. If there is an odd number of values, leave the median out of both halves.
Q1 is the median of the lower half. Q3 is the median of the upper half. The interquartile range (IQR) = Q3 − Q1, the spread of the middle half of the data.
3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14. The median is 8, Q1 is 5 and Q3 is 12. The minimum is 3 and the maximum is 14. IQR = 12 − 5 = 7.
draft.remember: Order first, split at the median, then IQR = Q3 − Q1.

a.q: Seven students read this many books last term: 4, 9, 2, 7, 5, 11, 6. What is the IQR?
a.why: In order the data is 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11. The median is 6, Q1 is 4 and Q3 is 9, so IQR = 9 − 4 = 5. Using 9 is tempting, but that is the range (11 − 2), which uses the minimum and maximum instead of the quartiles.
a.clue: Put the values in order before you find any quartile.

b.q: Waiting times at a Hobart clinic, in minutes, are 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20. What is the IQR?
b.why: There are 8 values, so the lower half is 3, 5, 6, 8 and the upper half is 10, 12, 15, 20. Q1 = 5.5 and Q3 = 13.5, so IQR = 13.5 − 5.5 = 8. The value 13.5 is only Q3, and 17 is the range.
b.clue: With 8 values, split into two halves of 4 and find the middle of each.

check.summary: No problems found. The card example and both answers are correct: IQR 5 for (a) and 8 for (b), with the distractors matching common errors such as using the range or Q3 alone.
